title: Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M — llama.cpp on 16 GB and 24 GB Macs
slug_note: The card's own llama-server command: 5.63 GB weights + 8192-token context, inside every Apple budget from 10.7 GB up.

variation.quant_detail: qwen35-9b-Q4_K_M.gguf (5.63 GB, HF tree), self-quantized from Qwen's original weights with a per-tensor imatrix

engine.config: llama.cpp llama-server on Apple Metal; -hf pulls the Q4_K_M quant directly, --jinja applies the Qwen3.5 chat template, -c 8192 context.

requirements.notes: Estimate: 5.63 GB Q4_K_M file + 8192-token KV ≈ 6.5 GB resident — fits the ~10.7 GB default Metal budget of a 16 GB Mac and the 16 GiB budget of a 24 GB one. Wider context pushes into the budget; the 24 GB tier's notes say Q4 32B files fail at 16 GiB, so keep context modest here.

steps.text: Install llama.cpp (brew install llama.cpp on macOS; see Step 0 in Quick start).
Open the local Web UI or point a client at the served OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

caveats: No laptop measurement recorded: status untested. The exact command ran as written on our DGX Spark on 2026-11-16; that box's speeds do not carry over to Apple Silicon.
The repo ships text-only quants — it carries no vision projector, so this lane has no image input even though the base model is multimodal.
The card insists on --jinja: without the chat template the model can emit malformed turns.

sources.note: card's Get started section states the llama-server command verbatim; quant sizes from the repo tree
